name: Austria

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 9197213 inhabitants, recorded as 9.197 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Still an opening estimate. Researched on 2026-07-28, in German, in the transversal venues pass; it forced the backing ruling settled the same day and then failed to close under it, for a reason worth keeping. Austria is the country that made the denominator say what backing means. It has almost no puppetry in public ownership: the work is carried by associations and companies that hold their own houses on public money. Judged on founding or ownership Austria counts nought or one, which is false about the country and would have applied a stricter test to Vienna than the German pass applied to Leipzig. The ruling of 2026-07-28 answers that — structural support counts at any level, project money never does — and adds the clause Austria itself exposed: the support has to be read in a document the authority publishes. That second clause is what blocks the count, and the block is about Austrian publication and not about Austrian puppetry. What is established: Figurentheater LILARUM plays in its own house at Göllnergasse 8 in Vienna, reopened for that purpose in 1997 after a full reconstruction, and shows Stadt Wien Kultur and the federal arts ministry as funders on its own site — a logo, which the ruling does not accept. The Salzburger Marionettentheater, founded 1913, plays in its own house; it is a GmbH whose shares went into a non-profit association in 2019, when the city, the Land and the International Salzburg Association took an Ausfallshaftung of 300 000 euros and the city advanced money so the puppeteers could be paid — a rescue, read in the Salzburger Nachrichten, which is a newspaper and not the authority, and a guarantee for one year is not a structural subsidy either. The Linzer Puppentheater has played since 1970 and holds a fixed stage and rehearsal rooms in the Kuddelmuddel, which is a facility of LIVA and therefore an enterprise of the City of Linz, the closest thing in the country to a stage inside a public organisation; the council decision granting it money is archived and returns 404. The Wiener Urania-Puppentheater has played in the Urania since 1950 with a continuous ensemble and was bought privately by André Heller in 2019 for 100 000 euros, so it fails on backing unless a subsidy is found. The Schubert Theater in Vienna carries a figure-theatre ensemble and is private. One number was seen and is not used: a multi-year award of 600 000 euros to Theater Lilarum GmbH, 300 000 for 2024 and 300 000 for 2025, decided by Vienna's Gemeinderatsausschuss für Kultur und Wissenschaft. It appeared only in a search-engine summary. Under rule 3 of this repository that is not a source, and it is left here as the thing to go and read rather than as a fact. If it holds, LILARUM counts. So the pass stops on documents, not on judgement, and the documents are named: Vienna's Kunst-, Kultur- und Wissenschaftsbericht, which the MA 7 says carries every subsidy of past years and which lives in the Wienbibliothek Digital; the minutes of the Gemeinderatsausschuss für Kultur und Wissenschaft for the Lilarum and Schubert Theater awards; the Linz Gemeinderat decision and the Amtsblatt for the Linzer Puppentheater; the Salzburg city and Land subsidy decisions since the 2019 rescue. Expect three or four when they are read, and expect the count to be a statement about Austrian budget transparency as much as about Austrian puppetry. The estimate of 2.5 stands untouched and remains worthless.

Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language, revised the same day after the ownership ruling and to record the candidate the first pass had examined without writing it down. No establishment retained. The mdw, the University of Music and Performing Arts in Vienna and the main public institution in the field, was re-read at source, this time on its own site rather than an encyclopaedic entry: its institutes cover composition, conducting, the individual instruments, singing and music theatre, popular and early music, music pedagogy, ethnomusicology and music therapy, plus the Max Reinhardt Seminar for drama and directing and the Filmakademie. No institute of figure theatre, puppetry or object theatre. It is now recorded as an examined and set-aside candidate, which is what the record was missing: it awards state-recognised degrees, simply not in this field, so its reason is outside_denominator. One sentence of the earlier reasoning is withdrawn. It read that the only Austrian offerings found belong to private bodies outside the denominator, which was a valid ground this morning and is not one any more: private bodies are no longer outside by construction, only when they award nothing the State recognises. Those offerings were never opened, so nothing is known about their awards and no claim about them is carried here. Confidence stays at estimated, and not because of the ruling. A source establishing that one institution has no puppetry institute does not establish that the country has no such course; an absence cannot be sourced the way a presence can. Upper bound held at 1: the universities of Graz and Linz were not checked, and the private offerings now need checking too. A trap avoided along the way, kept on record: the Figurentheater-Kolleg, which search engines return on an Austrian query, is in Bochum, Germany, and has nothing to do with this country.

establishments.name: mdw — Universität für Musik und darstellende Kunst Wien
establishments.award: State-recognised degrees across 25 institutes; no puppetry, figure theatre or object theatre institute among them
establishments.description: Austria's main public higher education institution for music and the performing arts, holding the Max Reinhardt Seminar for drama and the Filmakademie. Examined and set aside: it awards state-recognised degrees but none in this field, no institute of figure theatre or puppetry appearing among its twenty-five.

observations.reasoning: DISPUTED. First value produced as a mean conditioned on artists who actually tour, which drops from the denominator the makers who do not perform. Method error identified: a fee is not a performance. For France the true median probably sits between 10 and 20, over a bimodal distribution. For countries with permanent companies, recomputed from the top: 250 to 400 performances a year, casts of 3 to 5, a company of about twenty, so on the order of 50 to 90. To be redone in full once the denominator is settled.

performances: the Werkstatistik of the Deutscher Bühnenverein was read on 2026-07-27 and covers Austria alongside Germany and Switzerland, but publishes the split as Germany against the D-A-CH total only. The residual is 24 puppet performances for Austria and Switzerland together, which cannot be divided and is in any case a statement about which Austrian theatres file returns to a German association. An Austrian source is needed; none was looked for.
